==Errors==
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=1m02s|text=1:02}} [[Rand]] did not “spend time” with [[Thom Merrilin]] while in the [[Stone of Tear]]. They had one very quick conversation after which Thom deliberately avoided Rand to more effectively operate on Rand's behalf. Thom slipped him notes and such to give him useful information, but this time (unlike, say, the trip to [[Whitebridge]]) was certainly not filled with mentor-mentee tutelage.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=1m41s|text=1:41}} [[Rand]] got three questions answered by the [[Aelfinn]], not two. Nothing in {{4|14}} indicates two questions, nor does anything in Rand's internal thoughts throughout the series.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=3m16s|text=3:16}} [[Rhuidean]] is ''not'' the only permanent settlement in the [[Aiel Waste]]. The [[Aiel]] are not nomadic. Just about every Aiel settlement in the Waste is permanent. They live in holds, not camps (temporary “fairs” like those that occur when chiefs meet at [[Alcair Dal]] notwithstanding). In fact, one could argue that Rhuidean is the only known settlement that isn't “permanent” since no one lived there for centuries prior to the events of {{4}}. This can be fixed by replacing “permanent settlement” with “city” (as is done at {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=4m22s|text=4:22}}). Even if one quibbles about the definition of “city,” the books repeatedly describe Rhuidean as the only city in the Waste.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=5m19s|text=5:19}} The ''[[ter'angreal]]'' that shows the [[Aiel]] history is a [[Glass columns|“forest” of crystal columns]], not a solitary column.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=6m30s|text=6:30}} [[Mat]] did ''not'' “understand what this world was all about.” Mat can be very shrewd, but in this instance he definitely failed upward and did not cleverly figure anything out.{{ref/book|4|24}}
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=8m36s|text=8:36}} [[Kadere|Kadere's]] peddlers joined [[Rand|Rand's company]] days before they reached [[Cold Rocks Hold]], not ''at'' Cold Rocks Hold.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=9m05s|text=9:05}} [[Wise One|Wise Ones]] also knew the true [[Aiel]] history, not just the [[clan chief|clan chiefs]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=9m37s|text=9:37}} [[Lanfear]] visited [[Rand]] in the [[Stone of Tear|Stone]], but the visit was brief. She spent on the order of 10 minutes with him and only a few hours in the Stone as far as we know. She did not “stay around” Rand “during his residency” at the Stone. More importantly, Lanfear was ''not'' [[Selande]]. Selande was a member of [[Cha Faile]] (after being rejected by Rand as one of [[Colavaere|Colavaere's]] enticements). Doubtless the video is supposed to say [[Keille Shaogi]] instead of Selande.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=11m27s|text=11:27}} [[Mat]] did not take part in planning the [[Second Battle of Cairhien|battle of Cairhien]]. The chiefs did (and it's unlikely [[Weiramon]] contributed meaningfully) with possibly some input from others like [[Rand]] or [[Lan]]. What Mat did was basically re-create their plan while killing time waiting for Rand later on. This is significant because it's when Mat's tactical skills are fully revealed to Rand (and Lan) who had heretofore only gotten hints of it from some offhand comments by Mat.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=13m44s|text=13:44}} [[Mat]] did '''''not''''' just decide to take command because the [[wetlander]] forces were inexperienced. Mat gave them a tactical plan to deal with the impending [[Shaido]] ambush and intended to leave immediately. He only agreed to take command when [[Talmanes]] made it a condition of executing Mat's plan.{{ref/book|6|43}}
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=15m36s|text=15:36}} Setting aside the grammatical issues of dropping several articles, the narration outlines a scheme of [[Mat|Mat's]] involving himself and [[wetlander]] troops yet the animation shows [[Rand]] and [[Aiel]] forces falling back to lure the [[Shaido]] in. Mat and Rand had no communication during the battle.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=16m57s|text=16:57}} [[Mat]] did not suggest an attack on [[Caemlyn]]. He brought news of [[Morgase|Morgase's]] supposed death, which prompted [[Rand]] to decide to attack Caemlyn. This certainly wasn't a demonstration of Mat's skills.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=17m34s|text=17:34}} [[Mat]] did not “decide” to confer with [[Rand]] on a response to [[Morgase|Morgase's]] “death”. He just told Rand about the death without any particular intention of discussing or participating in a response.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=17m11s|text=17:11}} “Resolved” is a strong word.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=17m25s|text=17:25}} The wording implies [[Alviarin|Alviarin's]] letter ordered [[Rand]] to come to the [[White Tower]], which it absolutely did not. The wording also implies [[Elaida]] ordered Rand to the Tower, but technically she didn't (though that is splitting hairs).

==Nitpicks==
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=0m29s|text=0:29}} It's the [[Stone of Tear]], not "Stone of Tears." It's named for the nation of [[Tear]] in which the Stone is located, not because of how living in a power-wrought structure makes [[High Lord|High Lords]] weep.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=1m10s|text=1:10}} The [[Stone of Tear|Stone]] is a single monolithic structure. It has storerooms, not "warehouses."
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=1m22s|text=1:22}} The illustratiom of the redstone doorway ter'angreal is problematic. First, while it's probably not possible to properly illustrate the doorway, it would certainly be better to have something visually weird about the structure (maybe at least have the posts twisted or something). Second, the opening should be roughly rectangular or at least come close to the ground. As shown, it is highly unlikely anyone could step through, much less fall halfway through while trying to move it.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=1m36s|text=1:36}} [[Moiraine]] was also in the realm of the [[Aelfinn]] at the same time as [[Rand]] and [[Mat]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=3m32s|text=3:32}} While [[Rand]] technically sent the disloyal nobles away from the [[Stone of Tear|Stone]], he also sent them out of the country entirely. [[Tear]] is only ever referred to as Tear, not “the Tear.”
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=3m40s|text=3:40}} There seems to be some missing narration here. Captions seem to confirm this.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=4m03s|text=4:03}} The [[Heart of the Stone]] is not called “the Heart of Stone.” The name refers to its location (within the fortress), not referencing the material from which it's made.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=4m11s|text=4:11}} This is the second time “being taken over” has been used in reference to ''[[Callandor]]'', which is a really weird phrasing. While one certainly might refer to people “taking over” the [[Stone of Tear|Stone]], ''Callandor'' is just an object. One wouldn't say people “take over” Excalibur, for example. They'd just “take” it. It's not, say, {{Wlink|stormlightarchive|Nightblood}}; it doesn't have a consciousness or will and so can't be “taken over” in the sense that a ghost/demon might be said to “take over” a person.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=6m14s|text=6:14}} The information is correct, but probably confusing to anyone unfamiliar with the scene. He didn't so much “request” those things as simply say he wanted them in the process of venting his frustration at the (previous) Aelfinn answers.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=7m27s|text=7:27}} ''Technically'' the quoted words (“Thus is…”) aren't literally inscribed on the ''[[ashandarei]]''. That quote is a translation of the Old Tongue inscription on the weapon.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=7m35s|text=7:35}} It may not be completely accurate to refer to [[Rand|Rand's]] dragon markings as tattoos. They're definitely supernatural in nature and another character does eventually actually tattoo a copy of them which has [[Mangin|repercussions]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=8m16s|text=8:16}} “United them on [[Tarmon Gai'don]]” is a really odd way to describe [[Rand|Rand's]] intentions, since he united them long before Tarmon Gai'don. Perhaps this was meant to say “for” Tarmon Gai'don.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=8m27s|text=8:27}} Holds and septs are not interchangeable. Holds are physical locations and structures; septs are the people (kin group) that inhabit a hold. [[Cold Rocks Hold]] is a hold for the [[Nine Valleys]] sept.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=8m41s|text=8:41}} To clarify, “canyon” here refers to [[Alcair Dal]], not [[Cold Rocks Hold]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=8m44s|text=8:44}} Technically [[Couladin]] did not name himself [[Car'a'carn]] (or show dragon “tattoos”) until [[Rand]] arrived. When Rand arrived, [[Sevanna]] was still trying to gain permission for Couladin to speak so that he could make his claim.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=9m17s|text=9:17}} [[He Who Comes With The Dawn]] is never referred to as “The One Who Comes With The Dawn.”
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=9m41s|text=9:41}} Saying [[Rand]] “turned to” [[Lanfear]] implies that he sought her out. The text literally says Rand “turned to face [[Lanfear]]” when she appears, but this is merely describing his physical motion.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=10m10s|text=10:10}} The pronouns repeatedly refer to [[Lanfear]] as “he” which she decidedly is not. Alternatively, perhaps the "he" refers to [[Rand]], but in that case it is inaccurate because Rand did not do those things.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=10m18s|text=10:18}} [[Alcair Dal]] is never referred to as “the Alcair Dal.” More importantly, [[Sevanna]] was never truly a [[Wise One]]. She is treated like a Wise One by other Wise Ones, but only after [[Couladin|Couladin's]] death, and certainly not before Couladin had even left the [[Waste]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=10m36s|text=10:36}} The animation (and by omission, the narration) implies that [[Rand]] pursued [[Couladin]] from [[Alcair Dal]] to [[Cairhien]]. Rand brought his [[Aiel]] to [[Rhuidean]] while Couladin spent time gathering forces and speaking against Rand. Then when Couladin departed for Cairhien, Rand pursued from Rhuidean. In fact, it's in Rhuidean where the [[Darkhound|Darkhounds]] attack.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=11m13s|text=11:13}} “Five miles” is ridiculous and perhaps is a result of mistakenly conflating [[Weiramon|Weiramon's]] reunion with [[Rand]] with the layout of the [[Second Battle of Cairhien]]. Weiramon joined Rand somewhere between the [[Spine of the World]] and the city of [[Cairhien]], but it almost certainly wasn't as near as “five miles.”
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=11m53s|text=11:53}} To clarify, the other (unaligned) [[Aiel]] clans were present (hence why [[Rand]] was forced to split his forces). Perhaps there's another missing line of narration.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=11m58s|text=11:58}} "Tairenians" and "Cairhienians" are a completely nonsensical demonyms and it is very bizarre that they are introduced after so many correct references to [[Tear|Tairens]] and [[Cairhienin]]. Cairhienin is both singular and plural; Cairhienens is not a word, much less Cairhienians.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=13m05s|text=13:05}} ''[[Far Dareis Mai]]'' is not "Far Dareis Mar."
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=14m56s|text=14:56}} The "squad" consisted of three thousand soldiers.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=15m10s|text=15:10}} [[Sammael]] ruled [[Illian]]. He could not possibly have been in Illian while channeling lightning bolts around [[Cairhien]].
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=17m44s|text=17:44}} “Thwarted” is a strong word.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=17m51s|text=17:51}} This is not [[Aviendha|Aviendha's]] first appearance in the video and it's odd to describe her as though she's being introduced.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=18m57s|text=18:57}} “A huge [[balefire]]” is bad grammar: “a huge blast of balefire” or simply “balefire” would be more correct.
# {{YTlink|url=https://youtu.be/rDWpmzKjQ5w?t=19m18s|text=19:18}} “Carry the [[One Power]]” is not how one describes holding the One Power.
